title: Check yourself: Streaming tool use, errors in the middle, and when to stream

questions.stem: A client prints text as it arrives. Midway, an `error` event with `overloaded_error` appears although the HTTP status was 200. What is the right handling?

options.text: Keep the partial text as the final answer and finish the turn without more work
options.says: Ruled out because the partial text is the loss: "the user may already have read the partial text" and the answer is cut short, so it is not final.

options.text: Treat the call as failed, drop the partial output and send the whole request again
options.says: The page says "discard the partial output first and retry the whole request".

options.text: Ignore the event, since the status line already reported that the call went well
options.says: Ruled out because "A status check alone cannot tell you a stream succeeded".

options.text: Resume the stream from the last received byte once the service has recovered
options.says: Ruled out because a stream that failed midway "cannot be resumed from the last byte".

questions.stem: A team streams a long report only because they believe it lowers the bill. According to the page, what is the better reason to stream?

options.text: Fewer errors, since a started call cannot fail after its first byte
options.says: Ruled out because "That is why an error can arrive after the 200 status line".

options.text: A lower price for each of the output tokens
options.says: Ruled out because "Streaming changes when the bytes arrive, not what the tokens cost".

options.text: An exemption from the limits that apply to other calls
options.says: Ruled out because "Streamed calls count against the same limits as the others".

options.text: Readers see words while the rest is still being written
options.says: The page's first case is "A person is waiting for a long answer", and "The first words appear at once".
